messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P2 alert — Hosted runtime latency spike (p95 > 1800ms) for region-us-west. Pages sent to #eng-oncall rotation. See brief: https://console.redwood/internal/incidents/1865123456

Maria G.: I'm finishing a short handoff in ~3m. fyi the primary on schedule didn't ack; think they're in an offsite. There's a coverage gap until Alex or Rahul can flip.

Alex C.: I can jump in as primary in 5m if needed. can someone confirm whether this is runtime-only or infra-level (network/host)?

Rahul K.: quick look: the runtime metrics (kv-cache hitrate, batching) look normal. infra-level: node-level CPU on our GPU pool shows sudden increase on a subset of nodes. possible noisy neighbor or driver issue.

Jen P. (security-oncall): tagging security — based on initial traces it doesn't look like a malicious pattern, more like resource contention, but if you see repeated auth spikes tell me.

Chris L.: support says 3 active customers reported timeouts in the last 8 minutes. ticket links: https://support.redwood/t/98412, https://support.redwood/t/98413

Maria G.: ok, plan suggestion: Alex take primary runtime triage, Rahul act as infra secondary to investigate nodes. Sam please coordinate with support to collect example requests/times. If it turns out to be infra-wide, we'll escalte to platform pager.

Sam S.: on it — pinged the support on-call and asked for request IDs + customer impact matrix. will paste when they reply.

Alex C.: taking lead. first steps I'll run the quick runbook checks: 1) confirm affected model variants 2) check queue depth and batch sizes 3) check kernel/driver errors on node. Runbook: https://docs.redwood/reliability/runbooks/runtime-latency.md

Alex C.: running:
```
# runtime quick checks
redwoodctl metrics query "runtime.latency.p95{region=us-west}"
redwoodctl nodes list --pool=hosted-runtime-usw
ssh gpu-node-23 "dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i error"
```

Rahul K.: I'll start correlated infra checks: host CPU, mem, pci-e errors, and gpu driver logs across the pool. If we see NVML faults it's infra.

incident-bot: Update: alert group updated, P2 -> investigation. Pages retried to infra-oncall and eng-platform rotation (FYI).

Maria G.: careful — routing change means we might have duplicate responders. let's coordinate in this thread so ownership's clear. Alex for runtime, Rahul infra, Jen security on standby, Sam support. Chris can coordinate customer comms.

Chris L.: confirmed — posted initial customer blast to affected customers (templated). keeping updates every 15m.

Alex C.: quick findings: two nodes show driver restarts around the time of spike (gpu-node-17, gpu-node-23). NVML logs show `Xid 79` repeated. Suspect driver/firmware flakiness leading to degraded scheduling and increased queueing latency.

Rahul K.: confirming — host-level OOMs or PCI bus errors not present. it's localized to GPU driver faults. I'll open a platform incident and add the node owners. linking infra ticket: https://infra.redwood/tickets/PRJ-6721

Jen P.: security: not a security issue. no anomalous auth. standing down but available if needed.

Maria G.: handoff note: since primary didn't ack earlier, I'm adding to the post-incident checklist: ensure the rotation phone numbers are up to date and that overrides have backup contacts. filing a quick follow-up.

Sam S.: support: added customer logs to the infra ticket and asked customers for retry timestamps. one enterprise customer requested ETA — sending Chris the template for targeted ETA.

Alex C.: mitigation: draining problematic nodes and shifting workload to healthy nodes reduced p95 to ~420ms after drain. I'll coordinate a rolling reboot for gpu-node-17/23 after hours; RahuI, can we schedule?

Rahul K.: yes scheduleable. I'll coordinate with eng-infra to perform controlled reboots and driver updates, request change window. adding platform-oncall for the change.

Maria G.: closing the immediate page: ownership (Alex runtime lead, Rahul infra lead, Jen security on standby, Sam support/customer comms, Chris customer updates). please add short notes to this thread when you hand over or complete tasks.

Alex C.: note for next shift: if primary misses ack, incident-bot should escalate to secondary after 2m instead of 5m. I'll submit a PR to paging config.

incident-bot: Acknowledged. Created paging-config ticket: https://ops.redwood/tickets/1865123470

Chris L.: customer update sent: "we identified intermittent GPU driver restarts causing increased latency; mitigation in progress; next update in 30m."

Maria G.: thanks all — I'll add this to postmortem starter and link infra ticket + customer impact notes. Rahul/Alex, please ping when nodes are fully repaired.

Alex C.: will update thread when rolling reboots complete. switching to secondary on-call status in 5m.

Rahul K.: reboots scheduled for 23:30 PT in the maintenance window. will run pre/post health checks and report here.

Sam S.: support confirmed 0 new customer timeouts in last 10m after mitigation. sending closure note to customers in 20m if stable. :white_check_mark:

Maria G.: last: handoff reminder — incoming shift is @Alex C. starting now; @Rahul K. stays secondary until 04:00 PT. I'll mark my shift as complete. Good job team.

Alex C.: taking over fully. thanks folks.
